posts:
For 14 years, 66,000 NAB workers were shortchanged on pay while profits soared, exposing a massive corporate governance failure.
Evidence: 169M owed, 7-yr delay, 2M fine
#Aletheia #Workplace #Australia 🌐

NAB reported underpayments to regulators and is repaying $169 million to staff, projecting proactive corporate compliance and remediation.
Stated Judgement: (+0.6, +0.5) — Productive Potential

The bank dragged its feet for seven years after reporting the issue in 2019, systematically underpaying 66,000 workers due to baseline payroll failures.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.75, -0.7) — Regressive Extraction

Verdict: FAIL — Fall into Destruction.

Integrity: Meaningful Distortion (Hypocrisy: 6.8, z: 2)
National Australia Bank admitted to underpaying 66,000 employees $127M across 14 years, agreeing to total repayments of $169M and a $2M contrition payment.

The Poison:
A record $2 million contrition payment sounds tough, but it represents a paltry 0.03 percent of NAB's annual $6.1 billion profit.
This is a WHO vs WHAT error: shifting focus to corporate contrition statements while ignoring the seven-year operational delay in fixing basic payroll rules.

Social Physics Analysis:
NAB executed a smart selfish maneuver: pocketing labor surpluses, delaying fixes for seven years behind administrative complexity, and offering a tiny fine as PR cover.

The Trajectory: The Path of Fall into Destruction.
Modal Dynamics: can be -> Won't be via Red Top.
Promising compliance while dragging feet on wage fixes inverts intent into extraction.

The Unavoidable Truth: Systemic wage underpayment persists when corporations fail to audit basic payroll compliance.

The Unavoidable Lie: A minor fine resolves years of withheld wages.

Alethekanon:
Corporate contrition holds zero moral weight when wage remediation takes seven years of regulatory prodding while billions flow in profit.

Awwthekanon:
Every worker deserves an honest day's pay without having to wait a decade or rely on regulators to comb through half a million payroll lines just to get what is owed.

Brothekanon:
Crazy how a bank can make billions in profit while accidentally underpaying tens of thousands of staff for over a decade and taking seven years to fix it.

Spirithekanon:
"Woe to him who builds his house by unrighteousness, and his upper rooms by injustice, who makes his neighbor serve him for nothing." Jeremiah 22:13 FAIL
Withholding rightful wages for years while hoarding profit violates basic human justice.

The National Australia Bank has formally conceded it underpaid 66,000 of its workers $127 million over 14 years, with some workers owed more than $87,000 each as the result of problems that dragged on for seven years after the bank first reported them to the federal watchdog

NAB will repay a total of $169 million to staff, including superannuation and interest. It will make a record $2 million “contrition payment” to the Fair Work Ombudsman to effectively settle the legal side of the issue.

The issues stemmed from NAB’s failures to check it was paying staff at least the legal industry minimum under its pay deal with workers, to track staff hours and to correctly apply entitlements such as penalty rates. The bank first reported the issues to the regulator in 2019, but failed to fully fix them and the problems continued until this year.

Fair Work Ombudsman Anna Booth said companies had to invest in getting pay right.

“That’s showing... respect to workers who, just because they work for a bank, doesn’t mean they’re wealthy,” Booth said. “They have to pay their rent and their mortgages and put food on the table for their families.”

On average, affected staff will get about $2000. Fair Work Ombudsman inspectors had to examine 550,000 lines of payroll data to verify the underpayments. They were spread between issues such as incorrect base pay for part-time staff, which accounted for $37.9 million of the underpayments; problems with fortnightly pay calculations, which was $16.4 million of the total; $5.7 million of insufficient superannuation for staff on parental leave.

Booth said that when problems at large companies were not addressed over a long period “they become diabolical”.

Numerous other major institutions, including universities, law firms and retailers, have confessed to large-scale underpayments. NAB made $6.1 billion in profit on $22 billion in revenue last financial year.

Despite the contrition payment representing about 0.03 per cent of NAB’s annual profit, Booth said it was appropriate in the context of the complexity of the issues, the bank’s work to fix them, and the number of affected staff.
